settings.semantic_comparison: identical popularity-bin and text-length quotas; nonzero-text eligibility

prespecified_ablation_rule.selection: unchanged pinned four-category macro validation HR@10 only

metric_definitions.embedding_collapse_score: (mean off-diagonal cosine + 1)/2 over sampled nonpadding item embeddings. Measures directional alignment, not recommendation diversity or catalog coverage. The legacy value 0 for catalogs with <=2 items is unavailable evidence.
metric_definitions.pos_neg_margin_mean: Mean positive-minus-negative logit at the same loader position. Absolute magnitudes depend on score scale; null means no eligible positions.
metric_definitions.pos_neg_margin_p10: Nearest-rank tenth percentile of aligned loader margins; null means unavailable.
metric_definitions.pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate: Fraction of aligned eligible loader positions with strictly negative margin; ties are not counted as errors here.
metric_definitions.pos_neg_small_margin_rate: Fraction of aligned eligible loader margins below eps=0.5; this threshold is score-scale dependent.
metric_definitions.pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown: Position counts remain measured; all category lists are empty because product categories are unavailable.
metric_definitions.training_fit_challenges: Training-only indexed targets h[t] use h[:t], truncated and left-padded, and features[:, -1, :]. Earlier target occurrences are legitimate inputs. Repacking changes absolute positions. Each rank uses one target and 99 distinct negatives excluding padding, target and every observed prefix item. HR@10 and MRR are training-fit measurements, not validation or test metrics. Counts include repeated draws of the same records, not independent users. The training sampler draws uniform negatives with replacement excluding the user's complete training history. The conditioned_uniform challenge instead draws without replacement excluding the observed prefix and target, so it is not an exact sampler reproduction. Popularity bins reserve bin zero for zero-count items; tied positive-count quantile boundaries are retained and ties enter the upper bin. Popularity-matched pools expand by nearest log1p(count) distance, breaking distance ties by item ID. Semantic and quota-random candidates share nonzero-text eligibility, popularity-bin quotas and prespecified text-length strata. Latest-text queries use the final history item; target-text queries deliberately use the known training target solely to construct distractors. Missing semantic queries are unavailable, with no fallback. Unknown relevance and possible false negatives limit preference-error claims. Training-count popularity, observed-timestamp decayed popularity and latest-text-only ranks are shortcut baselines; prefix shuffles and within-bin target permutations are descriptive controls. Timestamp popularity requires complete aligned observed training timestamps; otherwise its unavailable reason is reported. Its fixed reference is the latest training timestamp and its exponential decay constant is 180 days. Target permutations may be ineffective for singleton or identical-target groups; effective counts are reported. Positive random-minus-semantic gaps indicate greater confusability on common records; three draws are robustness checks, not confidence intervals. The fixed ablation trigger is recorded but does not execute training or establish validation improvement. Any ablation must retain seed 42, the host evaluator, all four routes, and account for diagnostics and retraining within the shared GPU budget. No review fields, item ratings/categories/prices/stores or latent simulator traits are used or inferred. These probes do not replace the native twenty-user full-catalog unseen-item recommendation workflow.
